title: Cornwallis Papers: Southern-campaign letters 'mostly in cipher' (Rawdon, Balfour, Tarleton, Turnbull, Craig, Clinton)
correspondents: Rawdon, Balfour, Tarleton, Turnbull, Craig, Clinton to Cornwallis
status: Catalogue says cipher / number cipher with no decipherment noted for most; some have en clair copies. Common-cipher key known (Saberton). Checked 28 Oct 2026: Not verified item by item; umbrella entry for Cornwallis Papers southern letters. Saberton's 2010 edition (Naval & Military Press) likely prints many decoded; needs a volume check. (could not be verified: see prior_art) Printed-edition check, 28 Oct 2026: Partly in print. Ross 1859 vol. I (Rawdon 2 May 1781 cipher passage printed deciphered); the other cipher-marked items in PRO 30/11/3-6, 68-69, 81-87 not checked individually. Umbrella entry. Ross is a selection and prints few letters to Cornwallis, with only a handful of '[In Cipher]' passages in vol. I, so most of the 63 items are not in it. Saberton 2010 unreachable. No per-item concordance made.
why: Large uniform corpus for testing the rebuilt Common cipher and for finding other variants.
